events.title: The Gregorian calendar takes effect
events.description: Friday 15 October 1582 was the first day of the Gregorian calendar in Italy, Spain, Portugal and Poland, following directly on Thursday 4 October. Protestant and Orthodox countries adopted it only over the following centuries.
events.html: Friday 15 October 1582 was the first day of the Gregorian calendar in Italy, Spain, Portugal and Poland, following directly on Thursday 4 October. Protestant and Orthodox countries adopted it only over the following centuries.

events.title: Pilâtre de Rozier makes the first human balloon ascent
events.description: In Paris, Jean-François Pilâtre de Rozier rose about 25 metres in a tethered Montgolfier hot-air balloon, the first human ascent. Five weeks later he made the first free flight.
events.html: In Paris, Jean-François Pilâtre de Rozier rose about 25 metres in a tethered Montgolfier hot-air balloon, the first human ascent. Five weeks later he made the first free flight.

events.title: Napoleon arrives in exile at Saint Helena
events.description: HMS Northumberland anchored off Jamestown, Saint Helena, carrying the defeated Napoleon. On this remote South Atlantic island he spent his last six years, dying there in 1821.

events.title: Cologne Cathedral is completed after 632 years
events.description: Kaiser Wilhelm I attended celebrations marking the completion of Cologne Cathedral. Begun in 1248 and left unfinished for centuries, the Gothic church was completed using its medieval plans.
events.html: Kaiser Wilhelm I attended celebrations marking the completion of Cologne Cathedral. Begun in 1248 and left unfinished for centuries, the Gothic church was completed using its medieval plans.

events.title: Mata Hari is executed by a French firing squad
events.description: The Dutch-born dancer Margaretha Zelle, known as Mata Hari, was shot at Vincennes after conviction as a German spy. Historians still dispute how much, if any, useful intelligence she passed on.
